params: {"title": "How DNS resolution works", "track": "networking", "level": "beginner", "summary": "What happens between typing a name and getting an address: stub resolvers, recursive resolvers, root and authoritative servers, and caching.", "why": "Almost every outage story has DNS in it. Knowing the path of a lookup turns \"it's always DNS\" into a short checklist.", "objectives": ["Trace a lookup from the stub resolver to an authoritative server", "Read the output of dig and know which part is cached", "Explain TTLs and why changes are not instant"], "sections": [{"title": "The cast of characters", "minutes": 10, "body": "A **stub resolver** on your machine asks a **recursive resolver** (your router, your ISP or a public one). The recursive resolver does the legwork: it asks a root server, then a TLD server, then the domain's **authoritative** server, and caches each answer."}, {"title": "Caching and TTLs", "minutes": 12, "body": "Every record carries a time to live in seconds. Resolvers keep the answer until it runs out. Lower the TTL **before** a planned change, not after."}, {"title": "Reading dig", "minutes": 13, "body": "Run `dig example.com` and look at the ANSWER section, the TTL column and the SERVER line. Run it twice: the TTL counts down because the second answer came from the cache."}], "quiz": [{"q": "Which server finally knows the real address of a domain?", "options": ["The root server", "The authoritative server", "The stub resolver", "The TLD server"], "answer": 1, "why": "Root and TLD servers only point onward; the authoritative server holds the records."}, {"q": "What does a TTL of 300 mean?", "options": ["Resolvers may cache the answer for 5 minutes", "The server answers in 300 ms", "The record expires in 300 days", "300 resolvers have it"], "answer": 0, "why": "TTL is in seconds."}], "tasks": [{"title": "Trace a lookup", "minutes": 10, "body": "Run `dig +trace example.com` and write down every server it asks.", "solution": "You should see the root servers, then the .com servers, then the domain's own name servers."}], "recap": ["Stub asks recursive, recursive walks the tree", "Answers are cached for their TTL", "Lower the TTL before a change"], "resources": [{"title": "How DNS works (comic)", "url": "https://howdns.works"}], "next": ["DNSSEC basics", "Running your own resolver"]}
